assessment_membership.source: C3-c authoring declaration (2026-09-27): this target is placed in the V1 placement bank's mitigation-formula set by this cut's authoring review. The declaration is made here — no authoring fixture and no external assessment export in this repository places this target, so the membership is this review's own and is recorded as such.

texts.text: A mitigate unit that grants partial agreement and withholds the rest, so the speaker's disagreement arrives as a limit rather than a flat no.

The phrase answers a claim or opens a qualified turn: Up to a point, yes — but the second half worries me. It is built with up to + the article a + the singular point, and the withheld objection follows after the dash or the but (I agree, up to a point.). Said alone (up to a point.) it answers with the limit and leaves the other person to ask what the reservation is. In speech the phrase carries a small fall in the voice on point, which is the limit doing its work.

The article is the drill: the phrase is up to a point, and learners produce up to point because their own language has no article to place; the stored form carries the measure word a. The preposition is the second slip — until a point swaps in the time conjunction and reads oddly. The phrase also has a literal extent reading (the water rose up to a point just below the window), which keeps its own clause and is not the mitigator; the pragmatic work lives in the answer position.
在某种程度上；部分同意（先同意一部分、保留其余意见，让反对听起来不那么生硬）

pedagogical_profile.rationale: Bands are the C3-c authoring judgement (V1 carries no calibration data): the phrase is common in discussion and interview talk, so receptive value and naturalness are HIGH; core utility and productive value are MEDIUM because partial agreement can also be delivered with a plain partly or with the concede-then-but family, and this phrase adds the answer-position move, a narrower slice. Productive difficulty is MEDIUM because the article and the answer position are what production has to get right. Transfer value is LOW: one fixed phrase. RESOURCE_PRACTICE follows the entity's own declared learning_intent ESTABLISH. Revisit when Calibration100 response data exists.

pack_overlays.rationale: A frequent qualified-agreement phrase of discussion and interview talk, so it carries high weight in the general fluency pack's coverage accounting; the shortfall records that it belongs to one register of talk rather than to general use.

Granting partial agreement before raising the reservation (up to a point, yes — but the second half worries me) is ordinary workplace language, so the unit has a real workplace use; the reduced weight records that the pack's own review has not placed it.

example_policy.policy: Present at most two examples per attempt, whole sentences only: the canonical sentence first; a SUPPORTING or CONTRAST sentence only after the learner has attempted the canonical form twice without producing it. Always show the phrase in the answer position with the article a and the reservation that follows it, never present the article-dropped or until-swapped form as a model of the phrase, and never present an ERROR_INSTANCE as a model.

typical_errors.error_pattern: up to point (the article a dropped from the stored phrase)
typical_errors.explanation: The phrase stores the article as its measure word, and learners drop it because their own language has no article to place; up to point is not a stored English form.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the phrase reads up to point with no article in the answer position of a turn.

typical_errors.error_pattern: until a point (the time conjunction standing where the stored preposition belongs)
typical_errors.explanation: The phrase fixes up to, and learners swap in until because the limit feels temporal; until a point is not the stored form and reads as a cut-off time.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the answer position carries until a point followed by a comma, a dash or a but-clause.

detection_policy.policy: Fires only on the learner's own produced English text, and only on a visible surface form: the article inside the phrase and the preposition in front of it. No model judgement and no confidence score participates (PRODUCT_CONTRACT §8.1: V1 does not treat a model's self-reported high confidence as an R4 certification). Each rule below states the positive direction it must match; the fixture with the same ordinal states a case the rule must NOT match, so every rule ships with a testable boundary. expected values are NO_MATCH (the shape is absent) and NO_MATCH_BOUNDARY (the words are the literal extent phrase of their own clause, so the mitigator is not in use).

detection_rules.rule: ARTICLE_DROP: match when the answer position carries up to point with no article, because the stored phrase carries a point.
PREPOSITION_SLIP: match when the answer position carries until a point, because the stored phrase fixes up to.

ACCEPTED_REALIZATIONS: do not match when the phrase stands whole in the answer position (up to a point, yes — but the second half worries me; I agree, up to a point.), including the bare answer up to a point.: those are the accepted realizations.
THE_EXTENT_READING: do not match when the phrase is the literal extent of its own clause (the water rose up to a point just below the window), because the mitigator is not in use there.

detection_fixtures.text: Up to a point, yes — but the second half worries me.
I agree, up to a point.
Up to a point. What did the second survey show?
The water rose up to a point just below the window sill.
Up to point, yes, but the second half of the plan worries me.
I agree until a point, but the second half of the plan worries me.
